_comment: Storage: the immutable, volatile, UTxO and ledger snapshot stores, the Haskell database and snapshot import, SCLS and Mithril (module storage). Its reference is ouroboros-consensus's storage layer and cardano-ledger's state encoders. Mapping it adds entries only: its code is under the format freeze (FMT-1). docs/design/correspondence-map.md says what an entry holds; scripts/check_correspondence.py checks it.

given storage.haskell.state.ConsensusCod.note: version 1 and nine fields, the ninth the announcement as encodeStrictMaybe encodeAnnouncedBy ([] or [[issuer, hash, size]]), the bytes the reference writes; the types differ: Praos2.State holds Praos's eight fields as a PraosState with the announcement beside them where the reference's record is flat, and the announced size is a Long checked to a Word32 on writing where the reference holds a Word32. The 11.1 layout has no Praos2 and does not write one. LeiosLayoutSuite reads the Praos2 state of a captured Leios devnet state (no announcement), checks each of its nine fields against the values read off the file's raw bytes, and writes it back byte for byte; it reads and writes the public testnet's state at slot 2,168,639 whole, whose Praos2 state holds an announcement

def storage.haskell.state.Params.codecIn.note: the 11.1 layout's Dijkstra parameters (35 items, cardano-ledger f649f975 eras/dijkstra/impl/src/Cardano/Ledger/Dijkstra/PParams.hs:423-459) are refused (DijkstraNotYet.LedgerState), which the reference decodes; 11.x never enters Dijkstra, its major-version cap being 11. The Leios build's 54 are read and written byte for byte, every era's parameters held in one flat ProtocolParams, each field at the range of the reference's field type

def storage.haskell.state.Wire.unitInter.note: a Rational in the interval's bounds, not a newtype over BoundedRatio; the numbers are read as Word64 from version 12 and as Integer before it

def storage.haskell.state.Wire.nonNegati.note: a Rational in the interval's bounds, not a newtype over BoundedRatio; the numbers are read as Word64 from version 12 and as Integer before it

def storage.haskell.state.Wire.positiveI.note: a Rational in the interval's bounds, not a newtype over BoundedRatio; the numbers are read as Word64 from version 12 and as Integer before it

class storage.FileImmutableStore.IndexCa.note: the reference's past chunks (an IntPSQ by time of last use) and their number, bounded at 250 chunks; here a map by chunk with an index ordered by (time of last use, order of use), and the number of entries held, bounded at 270,000 entries; the chunk appended to is held apart, in Current, as currentChunkInfo is. ImmutableServingSuite checks the approved policy; no suite compares it with the reference, whose bound it departs from by decision

def storage.FileImmutableStore.IndexCach.note: the reference adds a chunk, then drops the least recently used one if more than 250 are held (composed at getChunkInfo and openPrimaryIndex); here it adds the chunk, then drops the least recently used until the entries held are within the bound, and does not hold an index larger than the bound. ImmutableServingSuite checks the approved policy; no suite compares it with the reference, whose bound it departs from by decision

garbageCollect's decision: every chunk last used at or before now less the expiry is dropped; here by walking the cache's index ordered by last use, where the reference takes a view of its IntPSQ, and with the age taken as now less the use; the trace event (TracePastChunksExpired) is not emitted, as the store emits none of the cache's TraceCacheEvent. ImmutableServingSuite checks the expiry over time under TestControl; no suite compares it with the reference

val storage.FileImmutableStore.IndexCach.note: the past chunks' part of emptyCached; the chunk appended to is held apart, in Current

def storage.ImmutableStore#refOf.note: getBlockComponent for the components a point's index entry answers (GetSlot, GetHash, GetIsEBB): getSlotInfo finds the point in the primary and secondary indexes and extractBlockComponent answers them from the entry, the block not read. Here one method gives the entry's slot, hash, boundary flag and block number (which the reference's secondary index does not hold), found in the chunk's entries as the store holds them, and the chunk file is not opened (the reference opens it, Impl.hs 466-469). HaskellImportSuite compares what it finds, for every block and for another hash at each slot, with the reference's own primary and secondary indexes: the Preview ImmutableDB cardano-node 11.1.3 wrote, and a Byron-to-Conway database with boundary blocks written by the reference's encoding rules; the other suites check that no block is read

def storage.haskell.state.Envelope.teles.note: one Past per finished era and then the Current, 1 + era index items, the era of the current state its length, as the reference's; the telescope is built with Telescope.make, so the eras abut. In the Leios build's layout every era is read and written, Dijkstra among them (LeiosLayoutSuite: the captured Dijkstra states byte for byte); in the 11.1 layout a telescope in Dijkstra is refused both ways (DijkstraNotYet.LedgerState), which the reference decodes; 11.x never enters Dijkstra, its major-version cap being 11

given storage.haskell.state.LedgerFileCo.note: [era index, the era's tip], a Shelley-based tip [slot, hash, block number] and Byron's with the boundary flag after them, as the reference's NS of the eras' AnnTip codecs; the model holds one AnnTip with a TipInfo per era kind where the reference's is per era. In the Leios build's layout a Dijkstra tip (era 7) is read and written (LeiosLayoutSuite, the captured Dijkstra states); in the 11.1 layout it is refused both ways (DijkstraNotYet.LedgerState), which the reference decodes

val storage.haskell.state.ConsensusCodec.note: the ledger state of the era at a telescope's index: a Shelley-based era's [2, [tip, NewEpochState, transition, fourth field]] read into the mirror, Byron's ChainValidationState kept as the original item (not modelled, so written as read). Dijkstra's is read and written in the Leios build's layout, at version 12 (LeiosLayoutSuite, the captured Dijkstra states byte for byte), and refused both ways in the 11.1 layout (DijkstraNotYet.LedgerState), which the reference decodes

given storage.haskell.state.CertStateCod.note: nine items written by the node's parameters' codec (poolParams), so the bytes of parameters without a key are those written before (FuturePoolParamsCodecSuite, both layouts). Read by that codec, then as the reference reads the two fields it keeps unread: the metadata as DecCBOR PoolMetadata at the state's version (PoolMetadata.read: a [url, hash] record, the url bounded by the version and its text chunked only in the Leios layout from version 12, the hash chunked from 12 in both) and the account's network 0 or 1 (decodeAccountAddressT, Address.hs:930-948 at f649f975), each refused with a typed error; the owner decided on 2026-11-19 (asked 19:18:13Z, decided 20:18:03Z, #85 item 38) that the state read matches the reference here. In the Leios layout from version 12 the voting key is read where the third of ten items is a list (decodeStakePoolParamsFlat) and written as ten items with the key third (withStakePoolParamsFlatEncoding, through ConwayCodecs.poolFieldsWith); below version 12 it is not written, as the reference drops it. Keyed parameters have their relays read as the reference reads them (PoolRelays.fromState); keyless ones keep the earlier reader, which takes any array and keeps its bytes. Reading and writing the key was approved under the format freeze on 2026-11-20 (#54), V10 changed in place

def storage.haskell.state.ConwayCodecs.p.note: the flat fields with a third written after the VRF key hash, the voting key's place; the caller writes the list length and the key, where the reference computes both from the encoding version

def storage.haskell.state.NodeTypeCodecs.note: the ten items with the third read by the slot's codec: none for the node's parameters (refused as DijkstraNotYet.PoolParamsBlsKey where it is a key), the key for the state's parameters; the reference peeks at the third item's type instead

class storage.BodyWritten.note: with the points sqlInsertEbBody notifies AcquiredEb for, every point of the hash where the body was stored, returned beside what the write completed rather than notified on a channel

class storage.PointWritten.note: what sqlInsertEbPoint notifies and returns: the length of the volatile body (stLookupEbBodySize) of a novel point's hash, for AcquiredEb, and CompletedEbs

object storage.LeiosEbNotification.note: the notifications of a point write and a body write in the order the inserts notify them, the body's then the closure's, made from what the write returned

def storage.LeiosStore#writeEbPoint.note: returns PointWritten: the body size sqlInsertEbPoint notifies AcquiredEb with for a novel point, beside the completed points

class storage.ReceivedBlocks.Linked.note: the block's reference (hash, slot, number, boundary) and its predecessor, the fields of BlockInfo the iterator's path walk reads; the header's offset and size, which the reference keeps to read a header alone, are not kept. Evidence: the wire cases of ChainServerSuite assert each outcome of the reference's ChainDB iterator and BlockFetch server, as their source at the pins gives it, over a connection Scarab serves; no running reference node is asked

def storage.VolatileStore.openIndexWith.note: as mkOpenStateHelper and its validateFile, each file in order of number is parsed (parsedBlocks, as parseBlockFile: each block read in turn with its location and what is read from it, here the predecessor, as extractBlockInfo; the parse stops at the first record it cannot read, BlockReadErr), then its blocks are added to the index up to the first one already held, in an earlier file or earlier in the same one, whatever its bytes (addedToIndex, as addToReverseIndex, DuplicatedBlock); the file is cut at the earlier of the two, the files after it are read all the same, and the file being written is chosen as mkOpenStateHelper chooses it. What reading a record means is the format's: a record that is incomplete, fails its checksum, is not understood or is not a block (the received log writes no rollback record) cannot be read, and neither can one whose block the given check refuses (ReceivedBlocks.Check: the block decodes and its header names the point the record stores, which the reference reads from the block itself). Where the reference builds a successor index during the open, Scarab's index keeps each block's predecessor, from which ReceivedBlocks.links answers. The selected-chain journal's open (open, openIndex) keeps its in-order recovery, which replays rollback records in order (#1247) Where it differs, by the approved Deviations of the decisions register's two 2026-11-21 rows (#1247), which apply to the selected-chain journal too, since both logs open and write through the same code: the open refuses a name that reads as a file number but is not the writer's zero-padded spelling of it (1.log for 00000001.log), before any file changes, where the reference admits any name its file-number parser reads and recovers that file under the name it is listed under (parseFd, Storage/VolatileDB/Impl/Util.hs 45-74; mkOpenState and validateFile, Storage/VolatileDB/Impl/State.hs 319-330 and 412-417); and, in the append of the block that fills a file, the store it hands back forces the full file to disk and closes it, creates the next file and forces the directory to disk before it writes to the next file, a force whose failure fails the append, where the reference's nextFile closes the full file and opens the next without forcing either (Storage/VolatileDB/Impl.hs 574-603). The check the node gives it verifies a block's body against its header at every open, the approved Deviation of the 2026-11-20 row (ReceivedBlocks.Check). Two of its differences are approved Deviations (the 2026-11-21 rows of docs/decisions.md#genesis-storage-and-keys: the refusal of a name that is not the writer's, and the forces at rollover); ReceivedBlocksSuite checks part of that behaviour: the refusal of a name that is not the writer's, which changes no file, in both logs, and the roll at the block that fills a file; no test observes the forces themselves, their order or a failed force, and no suite compares any of it with the reference, which it departs from by decision. It also indexes each block's predecessor where the reference builds a successor index, an internal difference that no differential comparison covers, a Gap (#1261).

def storage.VolatileStore.parsedBlocks.note: the blocks of a file read in turn, each with where its record is and what is read from it, up to the first record that cannot be read (BlockReadErr, here also a record that is not a block, which the received log never writes) or whose block the given check refuses as undecodable (BlockReadErr) or corrupt (BlockCorruptedErr, with the hash of the block as decoded, which the check's refusal carries, as parseBlockFile gives blockHash blk, Parser.hs 102-107; not the hash the record names), and the offset where they end (#1247) Where it differs: one pass reads Scarab's framed records, decodes and applies the given check, and keeps no header context (the reference's pbiNestedCtxt); no differential comparison covers it (#1261).

def storage.VolatileStore.addedToIndex.note: the parsed blocks added to the index in order up to the first one it holds, from an earlier file or earlier in the same one, whatever its bytes: the index after, the blocks added, and where the first such block is with its hash (DuplicatedBlock), the file that holds it filled in by the caller from the files the index's blocks were read from (#1247) Where it differs: it answers the repeat's offset and hash, and its caller names the file that holds the block, where the reference returns the DuplicatedBlock error with both files; no differential comparison covers it (#1261).

enum storage.VolatileStore.Trace.note: three of TraceEvent's constructors, Truncate, InvalidFileNames and BlockAlreadyHere, with their fields; the reference's DBAlreadyClosed and DBClosed trace closing its handle, which Scarab's store closes through its Resource without a trace (#1247); each is emitted where the reference emits it, BlockAlreadyHere inside the put (putBlockImpl, Impl.hs 394), so a tracer that fails fails the put in both; the reference then closes its VolatileDB, poisoning its state (modifyOpenState, Impl/State.hs 157-197), where Scarab's log stays open (#1258)

type storage.ReceivedBlocks.Check.note: the block decoder and integrity predicate the reference gives its VolatileDB (volCodecConfig, volCheckIntegrity, volValidationPolicy), as one function the node passes to the received log's open (ReceivedBlockRecovery.startUp), given the point the record stores as well: a record it refuses cannot be read and cuts its file, as parseBlockFile cuts at BlockReadErr or BlockCorruptedErr. Where it differs, by the approved Deviation of the decisions register's 2026-11-20 row (#1247): the node's check decodes the block, checks the record's point and checks the body against the header at every open, where the reference only decodes by default (NoValidation, VolatileDB/Impl.hs 188) and checks integrity (the header's own and the body against the header) only with ValidateAll, after an unclean shutdown or when the operator asks for it (ensureValidateAll, ChainDB/Impl/Args.hs 154-167); the header's own integrity is not checked here. ReceivedBlocksSuite and FetchedBlockIntegritySuite check the approved check; no suite compares it with the reference's validation policy, which it departs from by decision

enum storage.VolatileStore.CutCause.note: why the open of the received log cut a file, with ParseError's constructors: ReadFailed for a record that cannot be read or whose block does not decode (BlockReadErr, its reason Scarab's reader's, ReadFailure, where the reference's ReadIncrementalErr is its CBOR reader's), Corrupted with the hash of a block that decodes and that the check finds corrupt, the decoded block's hash as BlockCorruptedErr's is (blockHash blk, Parser.hs 102-107), not the hash the record names when the two differ, and Duplicated with the hash, the file that holds the block and the file cut (DuplicatedBlock) (#1247)

class storage.VolatileStore.Cut.note: the Truncate trace: why, which file (by the name it is listed under, as the reference's FsPath) and the offset the file is cut at, one per truncation, told just before it is attempted (a truncation that then fails fails the open), two for a file cut at a parse error and then at an earlier repeat, as validateFile truncates and traces them; ChainStorage emits each as StorageEvent.ReceivedTruncated, at Debug as cardano-node 11.1.3 and ouroboros-consensus 808e40054's tracing give Truncate (#1247)

def storage.ReceivedBlocks.recovering.note: the open of the received log, as openDB opens the VolatileDB from its files (VolatileStore.openIndexWith): the names it does not read traced, each file validated in order and each cut traced just before it is made, the index built; the store answers a put of a held block with BlockAlreadyHere. Beside the reference's state it keeps Scarab-only state, a cache of recent bodies and the set of blocks refused since the open, and hands back the open's report (#1247) Where it differs: besides openDB's work it keeps a cache and the set of blocks refused since the open, and hands back the open's report; no differential comparison covers it (#1261).

class storage.LeiosBackground.Info.note: the fields of the VolatileDB's BlockInfo that copyToImmutableDB's certifiedEb reads (biHash, biSlotNo, biPrevHash, biHasLeiosCert, biLeiosAnnouncedEb); the announcement is its hash alone, its point's slot the block's own slot (announcementLeiosPoint, headerElId), and the other fields are not read (#830)

def storage.LeiosBackground.certifiedEb.note: ChainStorage's copy promotes, in one promoteToImmutable call after the blocks are appended and before the copy's collection is scheduled, what each copied block certifies (copyToImmutableDB, Background.hs 230-292), its lookup the copied blocks and the immutable tip before the copy where the reference reads its VolatileDB, which holds the same blocks then (#830)

trait storage.GcSchedule.note: the schedule of the received log's collections, as the reference's GcSchedule, which is a newtype over its queue (a StrictTVar of a StrictSeq of ScheduledGc) that scheduleGC, dumpGcSchedule and gcScheduleRunner take; here an algebra of those three operations (#schedule, #pending and #run, each mapped on its own), its queue a SignallingRef of a Vector of Scheduled that GcSchedule.apply allocates, as newGcSchedule allocates the queue (#1247) Where it differs: the queue is held behind the operations, not as the type's field; no differential comparison covers it (#1261).

def storage.GcSchedule.apply.note: the queue's allocation only, as newGcSchedule allocates its queue; the schedule's methods are mapped on their own (#schedule, #pending, #run)

def storage.GcSchedule#schedule.note: as scheduleGC: the entry at the time now plus the delay rounded up to the interval, in place of the last entry for the same time, else after it. Where it differs: it hands the entry back and its caller emits the ScheduledGC trace, where scheduleGC traces it itself; no differential comparison covers it (#1261). Both trace right after their enqueue (scheduleGC, Background.hs 576, ouroboros-consensus 82ecba329), so a tracer that fails propagates out of the step that copied the blocks in both; the reference has signalled its ledger maintenance by then, where Scarab brings its backing store forward after the trace. It is called once for each persisted extension that copies blocks to the immutable store, where the reference's copy runner copies the whole prefix then eligible and schedules once: a Gap, #1262

def storage.GcSchedule.timeFor.note: the time is rounded on the monotonic clock in nanoseconds, the reference's in picoseconds; a time past the clock's range is its largest value

def storage.GcSchedule#run.note: waits for the time of the oldest entry, reads its slot after the wait, takes it off the queue and collects it, one at a time, as gcScheduleRunner; where the reference's runner throws in its linked thread, a collection that fails, or an exception anywhere in the runner, ends it with a value (ADR 0017), which ChainStorage hands to the node to stop on (#1247) Where it differs: it ends with a value where the reference's runner throws, and waits again when the queue is empty after its wait; no differential comparison covers it (#1261). Both trace PerformedGC right after the collection (garbageCollectBlocks, Background.hs 448), so a tracer that fails ends the collection's runner in both.

def storage.LeiosEb.encode.note: of any listed transactions, so that a body sent is hashed before it is taken for a body

def storage.haskell.state.NodeTypeCodecs.note: the era's codecs of the parameters (PParams.encodePParams, decodePParams); the 11.1 layout's Dijkstra parameters refused both ways
read by Dijkstra's decoder of a proposal at version 12 (DijkstraProposals.proposal); an action other than a parameter change written by the flat record's writer, which writes the same values

def storage.haskell.state.EpochStateCode.note: written as the reference writes it and read in its record forms; the reference's DecShareCBOR also reads a MemPack byte string for a stash entry's key and output (TxIn.hs:110-116, Shelley/TxOut.hs:162-174), which Scarab refuses

glue.reason: The block path's read of its read set, which a store may answer in part from entries it read ahead while earlier blocks were applied (the node's ReadAheadStore, #1484); the answer is always the store's read of the same keys. The reference reads a block's tables when it applies the block (forkerReadTables of getBlockKeySets in withValues, Storage/LedgerDB/Forker.hs at ouroboros-consensus 82ecba32), with nothing read ahead.

The import of a reference node's ImmutableDB is Scarab's own command, with no counterpart in the reference: which reference builds' Dijkstra blocks it stores (the Leios testnet's, whose chain is in Dijkstra from its first block), as bytes and with every other block's checks; no rule is applied by storing a block.

Groups Dijkstra wire codecs and validates constructed values by decoding their serialization with the production ledger decoder and comparing values. The encoded forms are mapped separately; these codecs are not persisted-state formats.
the decimal numbers in Scarab's own storage file names, written in ASCII digits under every locale; the reference writes the numbers of its own file names with show, which writes ASCII digits

the numbers of Scarab's own storage file names read back from ASCII digits only, and a name in a locale's digits, or a volatile log's name that reads as a number but is not the name the log writes for it, refused as a typed error; the reference reads the numbers of its own file names with readMaybe, which takes ASCII digits only, and passes over a name it cannot read, which its VolatileDB traces (InvalidFileNames) and Scarab's received log logs too

the frozen kinds of a stored script in the sidecar schemas of the snapshot versions before V10, and the script's codec over a kind's codec: Scarab's own persisted format, which keeps the bytes and fingerprints of its previous files; the reference keeps no such files and has no counterpart (#85, #54)

the frozen chain-dependent states in the sidecar schemas of the snapshot versions before V10, and the native codecs of Praos2's state: Scarab's own persisted format, which keeps the bytes and fingerprints of its previous files; the reference keeps no such files and has no counterpart (#826)
fills the parameters an era does not have from genesis, so that the node's one flat ProtocolParams is complete after an import; the reference holds each era's own record and has no such step (#826)

the ten items of a StakePoolParams of the Leios layout from version 12 whose third holds no BLS key, and their conversion to the held nine; Scarab's PoolParams has no key, so the reader that uses them (NodeTypeCodecs.poolParams, which cites decodeStakePoolParamsFlat, cardano-ledger 9df9f98c State/StakePool.hs:744-771) reads ten items through this record
plumbing: the immutable store's reads of its own chunk and index files (Scarab's own format) as an algebra with one interpreter over fs2's Files, so that a suite can count what serving a block reads
plumbing: the companion object that holds the empty index cache of the immutable store

plumbing: a fiber for the life of a resource that ends with its failure as a value (FIB-2), raised again where it is landed and at release; it runs the index cache's expiry, which the reference starts with forkLinkedThread (Index/Cache.hs 428-432, ouroboros-consensus 82ecba32), whose link throws a failure to the owner at once, where here the owner meets it at release; the expiry has no failure of its own

the admission of a ledger state that enters the node from a snapshot or an import, refusing one that no chain of the configured reference build reaches and that its rules would carry to another state than the reference's, and the snapshot format that applies it as a state comes in; the reference has no such check, no chain it runs reaching such a state (it decodes PState as it is, State/CertState.hs 257-265, cardano-ledger f649f975); refused rather than repaired by the owner's decision (asked 2026-11-18T08:22:34Z and decided 2026-11-18T14:21:46Z), docs/running/snapshots.md#unreachable-ledger-state

the store's own RocksDB layout of the Leios store format approved for #830 and changed for its exact round trip (a meta column family with the format record, and per partition the column families of the reference's ebs, ebBodies and ebClosures tables, the closure's written transactions, and the volatile closures' completion; opening, release and the in-memory rows of the volatile partition); the reference keeps the same records in its two SQLite files

what an import from or an export to the reference's SQLite files exchanges with the store, one endorser block at a time, the rows, body and closure of each partition as its tables hold them, through an open that resumes nothing, so a pending copy or sweep is exchanged as it is; the reference has no import or export of its LeiosDB
closed typed errors and their messages, where the reference throws a LeiosDbException with a message (ERR-1)
accessors of a body and of a status byte, which the reference reads inline from the vector of its LeiosEb and from the status column

how the store's RocksDB keeps the reference's guarantees: a read through a snapshot (the reference reads inside one SQLite transaction, dbWithTransaction), the volatile partition's rows held in memory with the volatile and copied ones a mark visits and the hashes with a marked row (its idx_ebs_sweepable and idx_ebs_markedForGc indexes), the size of a collection's batch, and the staging directory a new store is made in and published from by an atomic rename
a body's equality, hash and text, the ones its case class had, which it no longer is so that no product mirror can make one unchecked

the export's reading of the store from one snapshot, and a first open: under an exclusive operating-system lock on a file beside the store, a new store made in a marked staging directory and published by an atomic rename, and the parent directory synced before a store is taken; the reference reads inside one SQLite transaction, creates its files in place (initialiseLeiosDbFiles) with SQLite's own locking, and has no export

the permits that keep a process's first opens of one Leios store apart, one per lock file, before its operating-system lock is taken: that lock belongs to the process, so it cannot exclude another open of the same process; an instance the caller makes once for the process (EFF-4); the reference's SQLite files have SQLite's own locking, and it has no such permits
the import and export of the reference's SQLite files, which the reference does not have: their files, counts and the check that a database has both

how an import of the reference's SQLite files keeps them whole, which the reference, having no import, does not have: each file read inside one read transaction, so each partition is that file at one moment, and the store it fills built apart and published in place of the previous one once both files are read (by `import-haskell-db` only once the blocks are imported, so a source the target's chain is not in leaves the target's store), so an import again never merges into what an earlier one left
closed typed errors of the import and export and their messages, where the reference throws a LeiosDbException with a message (ERR-1)

the companions of the received log's collection schedule, and its parameters' constructor, which refuses an interval that is not positive (a precondition the reference states in a comment, roundUpToInterval, Storage/ChainDB/Impl/Background.hs 593-609 at ouroboros-consensus 82ecba329) and a negative delay

why the received log's collections stopped, carried as a value across the runner fiber's boundary (ADR 0017) for the node to stop on; the reference's runner throws in a thread linked to the ChainDB's (launch, Storage/ChainDB/Impl/Background.hs 116-121 and 140-142 at ouroboros-consensus 82ecba329)

what the received log's open found, its report and the cuts it made, handed back by ReceivedBlocks.recovering: ChainStorage emits the report as StorageEvent.ReceivedOpened, and each cut as it is told of it, through the open's callback; the reference's ChainDB traces the end of its VolatileDB's open with its newest slot (OpenedVolatileDB, Storage/ChainDB/Impl/Types.hs 829 at ouroboros-consensus 82ecba329)

the verdict of the check the received log's open is given, a block that does not decode or one that decodes and is corrupt, as the reference's parser tells a decoding failure (BlockReadErr) from its integrity predicate's refusal (BlockCorruptedErr): the reference passes a decoder and a predicate where Scarab passes one check; and Scarab's reader's reasons a record cannot be read, the payload of CutCause.ReadFailed, where the reference's BlockReadErr carries its CBOR reader's ReadIncrementalErr: Scarab's records are framed and checksummed, the reference's are bare CBOR blocks

where the chain database's background reads what it drives the Leios store with: the object that holds the promotion's block fields and their reading, and the Leios store's typed errors raised as the chain database's StorageError.LeiosStore, which the node's open of the store raises too; the reference's background calls its LeiosDB handle in IO, whose failures are exceptions (#830)

Why a stored value of a Dijkstra state's governance state is not a value of the era's types (#826), the decode error the state's codec gives with the era's typed cause: the reference's decoder reads the era's types directly and has no such step

The RocksDB UTxO store's own plumbing, Scarab's backing store of the ledger tables with no counterpart in the reference's UTxO-HD backends: the options it opens its database with, its batch read by each key's status, and its library failures as typed errors (#79).
